subject: Threshold breach — tail latency exceeded during peak; evidence & eligibility handoff
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@quickcart.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 22:18:00 -0700
Subject: API degradation at 18:05 UTC — spike in tail latency (Requesting next steps)

Hi Hannah,

We saw a significant tail-latency spike on QuickCart's checkout route around 18:05 UTC today — 99.9th percentile jumped to ~2.8s for a 7-minute window, while our SLO is 500ms. Traffic patterns were normal; no deploy from our side. Our engineers collected traces and flagged a sequence of repeated 504s and a handful of 500s.

Can Redwood confirm whether this meets the threshold for an SLA review and whether we should open a formal credits request? We need the raw request logs and any routed fallback evidence for our compliance audit.

Attachments: svc_trace_bundle_2027-05-03.tar.gz (traces), sample-req-ids.txt

Thanks,
Maya
Sr. Site Reliability Engineer — QuickCart

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya@quickcart.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 01:03:12 -0700
Subject: RE: API degradation at 18:05 UTC — spike in tail latency (Requesting next steps)

Thanks for the heads up, Maya — sorry for the disruption. Looping in Dylan and Karthik to validate the routing and autoscaler behavior.

Quick internal notes:
- Customer SLO: 99.9% < 500ms for /v1/checkout requests (per QCK-2741).
- Maya attached traces; looks like many requests were routed to an older instance pool that had a degraded kernel build.

Dylan / Karthik — can you confirm (a) whether there was an infra-side preemption/eviction in us-west-2 at ~18:03–18:10 UTC, and (b) whether automatic fallback to the region-mirror executed? If yes, we'll prepare a timeline and advise QuickCart on eligibility for a remediation credit.

If we need more raw logs, ask Maya which request ids to prioritize and we'll request a log bundle. I will also request a quick trace bundle from infra.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya@quickcart.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 10:22:44 -0700
Subject: RE: API degradation at 18:05 UTC — spike in tail latency (Requesting next steps)

On Tue, May 4, 2027 at 01:03, Hannah Schmitt wrote:
> Dylan / Karthik — can you confirm (a) whether there was an infra-side preemption/eviction in us-west-2 at ~18:03–18:10 UTC, and (b) whether automatic fallback to the region-mirror executed?

Quick summary after initial triage:
- There was an autoscaler hot-loop in us-west-2 between 18:01–18:08 UTC that saturated the local scheduler queue; two node reclamations were observed (preemption events at 18:02:35 and 18:04:58 UTC).
- Traffic was partially routed to the us-west-2 mirror (latency there stayed sub-SLO for many requests), but a subset of long-lived requests experienced KV cache miss storms once their model KV cache warmed on the mirror, producing elevated tail times.
- I pulled the router decisions for the sample request IDs Maya provided; ~42% of the impacted requests were pinned to the local pool during the first 90s of the window.

Next steps I recommend for QuickCart:
1) We'll assemble a timeline + raw router decisions and traces (see attachments).
2) Security wants to limit PII in the bundle; Maya, if you can mark which request ids are safe, send them over.
3) We need to decide whether to treat this as an SLO breach eligible for credit or as an operational noise event given partial fallback. My initial read: probable eligibility for pro-rated remedy because the local pool had preemptions and a meaningful fraction of requests exceeded threshold.

I can produce the evidence bundle by EOD PST if we agree on redaction rules.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Incident Response Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@quickcart.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 18:46:00 -0700
Subject: RE: API degradation at 18:05 UTC — spike in tail latency (Requesting next steps)

Maya — thanks for your patience. Short summary and asks: 

1) Eligibility: Based on initial evidence Dylan gathered, this appears to cross our SLO threshold for a partial pro-rated remedy because (a) the preemptions were infra-side and (b) ~42% of QuickCart's checkout requests in the window exceeded the SLO. We're moving this to formal review.

2) Evidence bundle & redaction: Dylan will upload the router decision logs, kernel event timeline, and trace snippets to the linked Drive folder. Please confirm which request ids we can include verbatim; otherwise mark them in the sample-req-ids file.

3) Postmortem: We'll produce a customer-facing postmortem and a technical RCA. Expected cadence: initial timeline + evidence within 24 hours; a draft postmortem in 72 hours. If QuickCart needs an accelerated SLA credit (pre-approval) to satisfy procurement deadlines, let us know and we'll route to finance for provisional processing.

4) Attachments sent to QuickCart: svc_trace_bundle_2027-05-03.tar.gz; smo-slo-matrix.csv (attached).

Maya — can you confirm receipt of this plan and whether you want us to open the formal credit request now, or wait for the full evidence bundle?

Regards,
Hannah
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
